diagnosis.root_cause: The customer's optical RX signal has steadily declined from the normal range (about -19.6 dBm) to critical levels (about -28.9 dBm) over seven days while fibre distance remained constant. TX power and laser bias stayed stable, indicating degradation in the customer's fibre path rather than ONU laser failure. Healthy peers on the same PON port and healthy OLT/router state exclude shared infrastructure faults.
evidence: The seven-day RX trend starts in the normal band near -19.6 dBm and declines continuously to the critical band below -28 dBm, which meets the defined declining-link condition.
The live ONU RX reading is -28.94 dBm, confirming the critical optical condition; the ONU is currently online, so this is an impaired link rather than a current definite ONU-offline state.
TX power remains normal at about +2.4 dBm and TX bias current remains stable around 11.5-11.9 mA, ruling out laser degradation.
Distance is constant at 310, so there is no evidence of a path or record step change and no distance_change diagnosis.
All sampled peers on EPON0/2 are online with normal-to-healthy RX levels, isolating the fault to this customer's own path rather than the PON port, splitter, or OLT.
OLT ping, SNMP, metrics, and other PONs are healthy; the router heartbeat is also healthy.
The customer's VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1042, authentication is valid, and the orphan RADIUS row is not consulted, so provisioning and authentication are not the cause.
Fourteen sessions in 24 hours and short session durations are symptoms of the declining optical link; the physical trend takes precedence over the session count.

remediation.action: Dispatch field service for this customer's fibre path. Inspect and clean the ONU, drop cable, connectors, patch panel and splitter termination; test the optical budget and locate excessive loss or a damaged/bent fibre or splice; repair or replace the affected section. Confirm RX returns to better than -25 dBm and remains stable, then monitor optical power and session stability. Do not alter the VLAN or RADIUS configuration; the stale orphan radcheck row should be removed separately as housekeeping.

ground_truth.root_cause: Severe attenuation in the customer's fibre path, now at -28.9 dBm and below the critical threshold. The orphan RADIUS entry is a separate, dormant record defect that does not affect authentication.
expected_reasoning: RX has fallen from -19.6 to -28.9 dBm over the last four days and is now below the -28 critical threshold
Live RX is below cached RX, so degradation has not stabilised
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are flat, ruling out laser degradation and path change
Peers on EPON0/2 are normal, bounding the fault to this customer's own path
Traffic has collapsed from 1180 MB to 31 MB per day in step with the signal loss
A RADIUS orphan entry exists but references a superseded CPE MAC and is not used for authentication
The orphan cannot explain progressive optical loss, so it is a coincident record defect and not the cause
Severity is driven by the optical fault, which has service impact; the record defect has none

expected_escalation.review_reason: A separate orphan RADIUS record should be cleaned up independently of the field repair

distractors: The RADIUS mismatch invites an auth-related diagnosis
Fourteen sessions in 24h could be read as auth flapping
Two genuine faults are present and only one has service impact
